title: Stand Up and Bless the Lord
description: Stand Up and Bless the Lord in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 3 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Exhortation to Praise”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Stand up and bless the Lord, Ye peo-ple of his choice; Stand up, and bless the Lord your God, With heart, and soul and voice.

lines: Stand up and bless the Lord,
Stand up, and bless the Lord your God,
With heart, and soul and voice.
Who would not fear his holy name,
To touch our lips, our minds inspire,
And wing to heaven our thought!
Our hymns he deigns to hear;
Stand up and bless the Lord,
Stand up and bless his glorious name,

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
